claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure and has not undergone post-solidification aging.
The proposed intervention is a solutionizing step followed by an aging step.
Aging at approximately 500–600°C for several hours will promote controlled precipitation of nanoscale intermetallic phases along lamellar boundaries.
An argon atmosphere will prevent oxidation during heat treatment.
The heat treatment will produce nanoscale intermetallic precipitates at lamellar interfaces.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates will increase interfacial cohesion.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation movement.
Aging-induced dispersoids will reinforce the lamellar boundaries.
Impeded dislocation motion will produce precipitation hardening and increase strength.
Precipitation strengthening will mitigate creep deformation under long-term loading.
Stabilized lamellar interfaces will reduce corrosion-crack initiation sites and improve corrosion performance.
Stabilized lamellar interfaces will reduce fatigue-crack initiation and improve thermal-cycling performance.
The aged alloy will have greater yield strength than the as-solidified baseline.
The aged alloy will have greater ultimate tensile strength than the as-solidified baseline.
The aged alloy will have greater ductility than the as-solidified baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit at least 10% lower creep strain under equivalent loading.
The aged alloy will exhibit a lower corrosion rate than the as-solidified baseline.
The anticipated operating range includes thermal cycling between approximately -40°C and 300°C, room-temperature constant loading, and salt-spray exposure.
Overaging or nonuniform precipitation could adversely affect ductility.
Failure to achieve the specified strength, ductility, creep, and corrosion improvements relative to an as-solidified control will falsify the hypothesis.
